div.div: أَعَقُّ مِنْ ضَبٍّ [More undutiful, &c., to kindred, than a lizard of the species called ضبّ] is a prov. [mentioned, but not expl., in the O]: IAar says, the female [of the ضبّ] is meant; and its عُقُوق consists in its eating its young ones. (TA.) [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 152–3. And see an ex. of أَعَقُّ in a verse cited in art. زهد, conj. 2.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
